_“20. Next, we now proceed to examine the prayers made in the Petition and the underlying issue(s) involved therein in light of the ratio laid down in the DVC judgement. On bare perusal of the prayers as well as grounds raised in the Petition, we note that the main prayer of the Petitioner was to hold and declare that the PPA stands terminated on account of force majeure and impossibility in terms of Article 4.5.3 read with Article 13.5 with effect from 05.02.2022 or in the alternate, hold and declare that the PPA stands frustrated on account of force majeure and impossibility of performance in terms of Section 56 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. All other reliefs are ancillary or consequential in nature. Thus, the main issue is whether the PPA is legally and validly terminated. We observe that, as per the ratio emerging from the DVC judgment dated 28.8.2024, such issues cannot be termed as ‘tariff disputes’ and, as a result, the adjudicatory jurisdiction of this Commission under Section 79(1)(f) read with Section 79(1)(b) does not extend to such disputes.”_

_“27. As already noted in the foregoing paragraphs, the main dispute in the Petition is of the termination of PPA on the part of the Petitioner. As already held by the APTEL in the DVC judgement that the dispute relating to termination of a PPA is confined to the legality and validity of the termination of PPA and does not relate to tariff or regulation of tariff, therefore, the issue involved in the present case also cannot be guised as a tariff dispute. The prayer seeking directions of reimbursement of_

_(i) The primary/principal dispute involved the Petitioner and Respondents in the present Petition does not relate to tariff or regulation of tariff and such dispute, thus, does not fall within the ambit of adjudicatory jurisdiction of this Commission under Section 79(1)(f) read with Section 79(1)(b) of the Act._

_(ii) As a result, the Commission is bound to refer such disputes to the arbitration in terms of the latter part of Section 79(1)(f) of the Act as the expression “and to refer any dispute for arbitration” used therein, as explained in DVC Judgment, definitely leaves scope for some disputes to be referred to the arbitration._

_(iii) Timely invocation of Section 8 of the A & C Act is not a prerequisite for this Commission to refer the disputes to the arbitration, especially when such disputes are beyond the adjudicatory jurisdiction of the Commission under Section 79(1)(f) read with Section 79(1)(b), as have been in this Petition._

_Keeping in view the nature of the dispute and the value involved in the Petition, the Commission finds it appropriate to refer the dispute(s) between the contracting parties to a panel comprising three arbitrators as per Regulation 49(b) of the COB Regulations, 2023. Accordingly, both the contracting parties shall suggest the names of the arbitrators in terms of the said Regulation within two weeks from the date of this order, and the third arbitrator shall be nominated based on the suggestions of both the nominated arbitrators.”_
